Best Protein Bars Without Seed Oils - Ranking 695 Bars by Ingredient Quality

We screened 1,298 protein bars available in the US for seed oils like canola, soybean, palm, sunflower, safflower, and several other seed and vegetable oils. The good news: 54% of protein bars do NOT have a seed oil on their ingredient label. We break down and rank the best protein bars without seed oils by category, brand, and macros. What "no seed oils" actually means

Seed and vegetable oils are some of the most common additives in processed food, and protein bars are no exception. This guide screens every bar for thirteen of them: canola, rapeseed, soybean, palm, palm kernel, palm fruit, sunflower, safflower, cottonseed, corn, grapeseed, and rice bran oil, plus any bar listing generic "vegetable oil" or "hydrogenated"/"partially hydrogenated" fat. High-oleic sunflower and safflower oil are permitted, since their fatty acid profile runs closer to olive oil than to the standard refined version of the same seed.

46% of the 1,298 bars in our database still have a seed oil on the label. Here is how often each one shows up, and where it usually hides.

Do Pure Protein, Perfect Bar, Built Bar, and IQBAR use seed oils?

Pure Protein and Built Bar use a seed or vegetable oil in every flavor we checked. Perfect Bar and IQBAR use none. Here is exactly which oils each brand lists, pulled straight from the ingredient label of every flavor in our database.

BrandFlavors CheckedUse a Seed OilOils FoundIngredient Quality
Pure Protein1818/18Canola oil (13), Palm oil (11), Palm kernel oil (9), Soybean oil (1), Sunflower oil (1)A–D
170/17NoneA–B
Built Bar1313/13Palm kernel oil (13), Palm oil (2), Sunflower oil (1)D–F
100/10NoneB

Pure Protein: 13 of 18 flavors list canola oil, and 4 other oils also show up on some flavors: palm oil (11), palm kernel oil (9), soybean oil (1), sunflower oil (1). No flavor clears this guide.

Perfect Bar: None of the 17 flavors use canola oil, sunflower oil, or any other seed or vegetable oil. The fat comes from nuts, seeds, and nut butters, or peanut/almond butter, used as whole-food ingredients, not an added refined oil.

Built Bar: 13 of 13 flavors list palm kernel oil, and 2 other oils also show up on some flavors: palm oil (2), sunflower oil (1). No flavor clears this guide.

IQBAR: None of the 10 flavors use canola oil, sunflower oil, or any other seed or vegetable oil. The fat comes from nuts, seeds, and nut butters, or peanut/almond butter, used as whole-food ingredients, not an added refined oil.

What we found screening 1,298 bars

46%
of bars contain a seed or vegetable oil
603 of 1,298 bars contain at least one of the oils we screen for. Palm kernel oil is the most common, ahead of palm oil and sunflower oil. It shows up in coatings, crisp layers, and as a base fat across brands at every price point.
Palm kernel oil is the single most common offender.
330 bars (25.4% of the database) list it, most often in a coating or crisp layer.
Only 0.6% list it as a trace amount.
Just 2 of the 330 bars containing palm kernel oil list it inside a "contains less than 2%" clause. In the rest, it's a real component of the recipe, not a rounding error.
Barebells disqualifies almost entirely.
23 of 25 flavors fail.
Whole-food bars dominate the qualifying pool.
RXBAR, Larabar, Thunderbird, Off the Farm, Healthy Eating on the Go all qualify at or near 100%. Their fat comes from nuts, seeds, dates, or coconut rather than a refined oil.
A mixed lineup is common, not rare.
29 brands we checked split meaningfully between qualifying and disqualified flavors within the same lineup. KIND is the starkest case: 6 of 31 flavors qualify.
144 brands still represented.
Even with 46% of the database disqualified, the qualifying pool covers a wide range of protein levels, price points, and grades.

Frequently asked questions

We screen for canola oil, rapeseed oil, soybean oil, palm oil, palm kernel oil, palm fruit oil, sunflower oil, safflower oil, cottonseed oil, corn oil, grapeseed oil, rice bran oil, and generic vegetable oil. High-oleic sunflower and safflower oil are permitted because their fatty acid profile is different from the standard refined versions.
No. All 12 RXBAR flavors qualify. RXBAR is built on egg whites, dates, and nuts, so the fat comes entirely from whole-food sources with nothing refined added.
Most, but not all. 26 of 29 Larabar flavors qualify. Most run four to six ingredients total, usually dates plus a nut or two, so there is little room for a seed oil to hide, but a few flavors do use one.
Some do. 6 of 31 KIND flavors qualify, including Fruit and Nut. The rest use palm kernel oil or canola oil, most often in a coating or crisp layer, so check the specific flavor rather than assuming the whole line is clean.
13 of 18 flavors list canola oil, and 4 other oils also show up on some flavors: palm oil (11), palm kernel oil (9), soybean oil (1), sunflower oil (1). No flavor clears this guide.
None of the 17 flavors use canola oil, sunflower oil, or any other seed or vegetable oil. The fat comes from nuts, seeds, and nut butters, or peanut/almond butter, used as whole-food ingredients, not an added refined oil.
13 of 13 flavors list palm kernel oil, and 2 other oils also show up on some flavors: palm oil (2), sunflower oil (1). No flavor clears this guide.
None of the 10 flavors use canola oil, sunflower oil, or any other seed or vegetable oil. The fat comes from nuts, seeds, and nut butters, or peanut/almond butter, used as whole-food ingredients, not an added refined oil.
Bars with a chocolate coating or crispy layer are the most common offenders. Palm kernel oil is the single most frequent culprit across the database, ahead of palm oil and sunflower oil. It often shows up as "palm kernel oil" rather than plain "palm oil," so it is easy to miss on a quick label scan.
No. Coconut oil is not screened out by this guide. It comes from coconut flesh, not a seed, and has a different fatty acid makeup than the oils on our exclusion list. Bars using coconut oil or coconut butter qualify here.
High-oleic sunflower and safflower oils are permitted. They are bred for a high monounsaturated fat content, closer in profile to olive oil than to the standard refined version of the same seed. They are not treated as the same ingredient for this screen.
Yes, and it is more common than you would expect. NuGo splits almost exactly down the middle: 15 of 30 flavors qualify. Larabar, Bobo's, and GoMacro all show the same pattern, usually because one flavor's coating or crisp layer uses a different fat source than the rest of the line. Always check the specific flavor, not just the brand.
We update the database whenever new bars are added or a brand reformulates. Manufacturers do change their ingredient lists over time, so always confirm against the packaging in front of you. This page reflects the database as of 2026-08-31.
695 bars across 144 brands clear our seed oil screen, led by whole-food brands like RXBAR, Healthy Eating on the Go, and Thunderbird that qualify 100% of the time. The full ranked list is in the table below, sorted by ingredient quality.
603 of the 1,298 bars we track contain at least one seed or vegetable oil. Barebells, Wonderslim, Pure Protein disqualify almost entirely, usually through palm kernel oil, palm oil, or sunflower oil in a coating or crisp layer.
Canola comes from rapeseed, which is a seed. We group it with the other refined seed and vegetable oils on this list for the same reason: a highly processed extraction method and a fatty acid profile heavier in omega-6 than whole-food fat sources like nuts, seeds, or dairy.
